lines.li: [them] So your colony holds of us now.
[us] It does, and we hope it's a fair bargain for both of us.
[them,their:tribal] The elders say a small fire burns longer beside a big one.
[them,their:medieval] Then you're under our lord's hand, and we'll treat you as our own.
[them,their:hightech] Then you're on our books now, for better or worse.
[them] Keep your side and we'll keep ours.
[them] Our collector says your gate is always open and the count always right.
[us] We'd rather pay it than argue about it.
[them] That's the right way to look at it.
[them] Your colony still owes us part of the season's tribute.
[us] It was a lean season, and we gave what the stores held.
[us,poor] We gave what we had, and there wasn't much of it.
[them,their:lowtech] Our head won't wait past the next season, and nobody can make them.
[them] Pay it before the season turns, or the oath won't hold.
[them] People who don't pay their tribute shouldn't expect our band.
[us] You'll have it, give us time.
[them] Your colony pays its tribute, and that's about all I'd say for it.
[us] That's what was agreed.
[them] So it is.
[them] You sent your people when we called, our fighters noticed.
[them,their:tribal] Your spears came when our horn sounded, and the elders saw it.
[us] We swore we would.
[us,us:hurt] I was one of them, and I've the scars to show for it.
[them] Plenty swear, fewer come.
[us] It's hard, sending our own to fight in someone else's war.
[them] It's someone else's war until it reaches your walls.
[us] I suppose that's the bargain.
[us] Your band came when the raiders were at our walls, we won't forget it.
[them] That's what the oath is for.
[them,their:medieval] A lord who won't stand by those who hold of them isn't much of a lord.
[us] It was worth every bit of the tribute that day.
[them] We heard raiders came at your walls again.
[us] They did, and we're still standing.
[them,fealty:protected] Our band said your people held their ground.
[them,!fealty:protected] Good, the people who hold of us should be hard to break.
[us] Does the oath mean your enemies are ours now?
[them] Our quarrels are ours, you only come when we call.
[them,their:hightech] Your obligations are in the terms, and that isn't one of them.
[us] Good, we have enough of our own.
[us,trait:Greedy] Every season the tribute goes out the gate and I count it as it goes.
[us] Not everyone here wanted to swear, I'll be honest with you.
[them] There's always someone who'd rather go it alone, until the raiders come.
[us] That's more or less what the council said.
[them] You've kept your side of the oath well enough so far.
[them,fealty:short] I'd think better of your colony with its tribute paid.
[us] We mean to keep it.
[them] Then we'll get on.
[them] Your gifts reached the elders' fire, and they were pleased.
[us] We call it tribute, but gifts sounds kinder.
[them] The words don't matter much to the elders, the meat does.
[them] The reeve counted your tribute twice and found it honest.
[us] Twice?
[them] The reeve counts everything twice, supper included.
[them] Back at the office your colony's file is one of the tidy ones.
[us] We try to keep it that way.
[them] Most protectorates are a headache, so it's noticed.
[them] Your account under the accord is in good standing.
[us] Is that good?
[them] It puts you ahead of most of our contractors.
[us] The tribute's hardest to find in winter, when the stores are low.
[them] It's hard for everyone in winter, ours included.
[us] I suppose it is.
[us] We don't pray the way you do, and some of ours mind swearing to you for it.
[them] An oath between peoples isn't a prayer, it's a bargain.
[us] I'll tell them you said so.
[us] I want my children to grow up somewhere raiders think twice about.
[them] That's why most swear, in the end.
[them] When I was young, a small place like this held of nobody and paid for it.
[us] Paid how?
[them] In graves, mostly.
[them] Strange to visit a place that holds of my own people.
[us] Strange how?
[them] I keep expecting someone to bow, and nobody does.
[them] Our kin at the town under your protection write home now and then.
[us] Good things, I hope.
[them,vassal:heavy] That your share of their harvest is too big, mostly.
[them,!vassal:heavy] That you leave them be, mostly, which suits them.
[them] Your colony takes a heavy cart from our kin every harvest.
[us] We protect them, and that costs us too.
[them,their:tribal] A guardian who eats the whole hunt isn't guarding much.
[them] Our kin say they're paying for protection with their winter.
[them] You bleed our kin dry and call it protection.
[us] The council set the share, not me.
[them] Our kin sent their fighters when your colony called them.
[us] They did, and they fought well.
[them] Then remember it the next time they ask you for something.
[them] We swore ourselves to your colony, and most of us are glad we did.
[us] We're glad of it too.
[them,vassal:heavy] We'd be gladder with a lighter cart at harvest.
[them] Keep your side, and we'll keep ours.
[them] I stop at the town you protect on my way here.
[us] How are they doing?
[them] Better than they were, and they say so.
[us] If your kin ever need a quarrel settled, the colony will hear them out.
[them] Better you than a fight at the boundary stone.
[us] That's what we think too.
[us] Is the fighting with {THEN} still going on?
[them] Still, and we may yet call on your colony's oath for it.
[us,fealty:levies] We came once already, and we'd come again.
[us] Then we'll be ready if you do.
[them] You told me about a raid last time, so send us word if raiders come again.
[us,fealty:protected] Your band came when they did, and we were glad of it.
[us] We will, and we're glad of the help.
[them] That's what the oath is for.
[them] You told me about your harvest last time, I hope the tribute left you enough of it.
[us] We manage, most seasons.
[them] Good, a hungry colony is no use to anyone.
